items.title: OpenAI just scooped mathematicians' work on another million-dollar problem
items.excerpt: Another bombshell result shows how artificial intelligence is fueling fierce competition at the frontiers of math and physics: OpenAI says its models produced proofs in mathematics, computer science and quantum physics, one of which touches a million-dollar problem.

items.title: Dueling proofs from OpenAI and Anthropic astound scientists
items.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic released AI-generated results that claim to resolve major problems in math, physics and computer science, but like other recent AI 'slop drops' the releases are already controversial among researchers. Same cluster as the OpenAI-proofs item; the curator should pick one.

items.title: OpenAI Computing Claim Faces Review, Raising Questions About Quantum Advantage
items.excerpt: Researchers will examine an AI-generated proof claiming to refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a long-standing assumption about how hard certain computing problems are, and the article covers what that would mean for quantum-advantage arguments.

items.title: SPINE: A machine-learning program is on the trail of ghost particles
items.excerpt: SLAC's SPINE runs staged machine-learning models that find features in liquid-argon detector images, identify individual particles and rebuild whole neutrino interactions. It underpins ICARUS's first search for sterile-neutrino oscillation (arXiv 2603.22557).

items.title: New neural framework could make LLMs more empathetic
items.excerpt: Georgia Tech researchers built a 'capability provenance' framework that traces which training-data sources drive an LLM's behaviour. Auditing Olmo 3, they found that stronger social reasoning and empathy came from interpersonal dialogue data such as FAQs and customer-service chats, not from textbooks (COLM; arXiv 2606.19625).

items.title: 10 minutes is all it takes for AI assistance to erode your motivation, study shows
items.excerpt: In a set of problem-solving experiments, people who used AI to get answers were more likely to give up and fail once that help was removed than people who never had AI help. A cognitive-offloading study.

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts, and one mathematician called the implications 'staggering'.

items.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics: the KLS conjecture
items.excerpt: A Microsoft Research scientist and a collaborator proved the 1995 Kannan-Lovasz-Simonovits conjecture in high-dimensional convex geometry. They worked with AI agents in a structured, human-directed process that explored more than 100 candidate approaches before finding a recursive criterion.

items.title: AI designs functional enzyme components that could help expand drug discovery
items.excerpt: HIPS researchers combined pretrained AI models with experiments to design 76 new thiolation domains for non-ribosomal peptide synthetases. Several worked in living cells, and some raised product yields up to threefold over natural versions (Nature Communications, 10.1038/s41467-026-77963-6).

items.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
items.excerpt: A recurrent neural operator with built-in memory of how the physics changes flagged a simulated collapse of low ocean clouds more than two years ahead, with a timing error of about 11 days. It also anticipated an abrupt loss of wing lift in airflow simulations (Caltech/CU Boulder/NVIDIA, PNAS 10.1073/pnas.2600331123). The page shows a date only.

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: UCLA researchers paired a digital encoder with a free-space optical decoder to score video authenticity. It reached about 97.8% accuracy on Celeb-DF batches while using less energy than comparable digital neural networks (eLight).

items.title: The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning
items.excerpt: Google Research adds a sleep phase to continual learning so that LLMs can keep absorbing new facts and improving their reasoning while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and fixed knowledge cutoffs. This is ML method work with a neuroscience-inspired angle, so it is lower priority for science.

items.title: New AI-powered mosquito trap could help curb dengue outbreaks
items.excerpt: A smart trap from the USF startup Digitomy uses built-in cameras and AI to identify mosquito species with more than 98% accuracy, supporting real-time vector surveillance during Florida's dengue outbreak. Low priority: it is applied surveillance.

items.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
items.excerpt: MIT historian Benjamin Lindquist argues that generative AI models are rooted in ideas from mid-20th-century engineers who thought some irrationality was essential for a machine that could think like a human. Low priority: this is history of science.
